faqs.q: Which assets can I trade?
faqs.a: 9 crypto assets through broker partners, per the published pages. The list varies between sections, so check the dashboard after signup.

faqs.q: How fast are withdrawals?
faqs.a: The page promises payouts within a day, but the processing detail is thin. Confirm the exact timeline and any fees with support before funding anything.

bottomLine: The verdict on the product is cautious approval: it works, it includes a demo, and it should be used with the minimum deposit while the claims are unproven.
The scorecard settles at 4.8. That is a cautious pass - proceed with the demo first, the minimum deposit second, and treat every payout figure as unproven until you see it yourself.

intro: Fintrad sells a browser-based AI trading desk with a US$250 entry. Before the first deposit, it is worth asking which of the published claims survive contact with the platform own fine print.
The offer is a dashboard, a set of AI signals, and a broker relationship. You fund US$250, set risk preferences, and trade 12 assets automatically or by hand, with the demo alongside.
The scorecard is the average of five dimensions, each scored from the platform own pages. Nothing in it is taken from testimonials, ads or the platform self-assigned rating.
whatItClaims: A partner broker holding funds and executing orders.
Withdrawals processed in under a day, per the page.
No prior trading experience required.
AI and algorithmic market analysis producing signals and suggested entries.
Automatic or manual execution, with a browser-based platform.
whatWeChecked: The deposit terms: minimum amount, payment methods and where the money sits.
The demo claim: practice account confirmed in the signup flow.
The payout promise: within-a-day wording without processing detail.
The broker relationship: which partner desk executes orders.
The asset list: how many pairs are actually offered.
The registration flow: what personal details the form collects.

faqs.q: Does it offer a demo account?
faqs.a: Yes - a practice account is part of the package and runs alongside the live balance, which is the sensible first step before risking the US$250 minimum.

faqs.q: What is the minimum deposit?
faqs.a: US$250, funded by bank card, bank transfer, PayPal or Skrill. It is trading capital in your balance, not a fee - and it is exposed to market risk once live.

faqs.q: What happens after I sign up?
faqs.a: You confirm the account by email, fund US$250, set your risk preferences and choose automatic or manual mode. The demo account runs alongside while you learn.

faqs.q: What does the published score actually mean?
faqs.a: It does double duty - a platform score and an early community response - and neither is independently verified. Treat both as marketing until proven otherwise.

faqs.q: Is registration free?
faqs.a: Yes - signup is free and activates through a confirmation link. The first cost is the US$250 deposit, which stays in your trading balance.

bottomLine: The platform itself is workable - the dashboard, the demo and the two trading modes are all present. The caution applies to the claims around them, not the mechanics.
The verdict holds at 4.8: research it, demo it, and if you fund it, fund the minimum. The platform earns a careful start, not blind trust.
